readings.title: This dazzling bird has a lethal parenting method
body: 5 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Diego Arguedas Ortiz Scarlet macaws are an iconic but declining tropical bird. To change the species' fate, scientists are working to counter a lethal parenting method that dooms many chicks to death. Parker hadn't even opened his eyes when a hand snatched him from his nest. It was a Monday morning in November 2018 in the Tambopata National Reserve, deep in the Peruvian Amazon, and the featherless chick was frail and underweight, barely longer than a middle finger. He was the youngest of his four scarlet macaw siblings, and that meant he was almost certainly doomed to starve. Standing at the base of the tree was Gabriela Vigo-Trauco, the Peruvian scientist who orchestrated this abduction. By studying these birds for over two decades, Vigo-Trauco had discovered that scarlet macaws intentionally starve their youngest chicks. The scientist from Texas A&M University found that almost all third and fourth chicks in multi-egg nests don't make it, and around 25% of second-born chicks meet the same fate. This brutal parenting approach was once a survival strategy. Now, it is a formidable constraint on recovery for this declining species – with poaching and logging already having driven one sub-species to near extinction across Mexico and Central America. In 2017, Vigo-Trauco launched a rarely attempted form of rescue-mission , which led her to the chick she named Parker . Her goal was to recruit wild scarlet macaw couples to become foster parents for the doomed chicks. By persuading wild birds to take on the task, she hoped to test out a new lifeline for Peru's neglected offspring – and for the wider species. Scarlet macaws are impossible to miss. Their crimson plumage stands out against the forest green, and you can hear their screeches long before you see them. Each female can lay up to four eggs per season, but usually only one or two fly from the nest. "The parents, particularly the mother, pushed [the youngest] away," says Vigo-Trauco, who is co-director of The Macaw Society, a Peruvian conservation organisation that first revealed this behaviour , after installing nest-cameras in 2007. "The chick is cold and screaming, and when the father comes, he feeds the mother, the [first and second] chicks, and leaves the third one yelling away." There was no sibling bullying, and no link to food availability. So why do the parents neglect their younger chicks? Vigo-Trauco believes parents can't cope well with chicks at different development stages. Even four or five days between hatching can make a huge difference, with the resulting chicks requiring vastly different feeding regimes and even nest temperatures. The parents are forced to choose, she says. If they stretch too much to feed them all, there's a risk none will make it. For the relatively healthy scarlet macaw populations of the Peruvian Amazon, the loss of younger chicks is less consequential. But in countries where conservationists fight poachers and loggers for every bird's survival, Vigo-Trauco says that the death of even a handful of chicks is a disaster. Raising rejected chicks by hand is one potential solution. But it can take between 1.5 to three months for them to fly away. Plus, parrots raised in captivity have notoriously low survival rates : they struggle to feed in the wild, identify predators and form flocks. So Vigo-Trauco's team turned to the idea of wild foster parents. After they seized Parker in 2018, Vigo-Trauco's team hand-fed him in their field station for three weeks, following a relentless two-hour schedule. They also screened the forest's nests to find the chick a suitable foster family, who would teach him how to live as a wild bird. The technique had been tested by aviculturists raising macaws in captivity in the past few decades, where conditions are controlled and swapping nests means walking across the hall with a chick. It also builds on experiments involving other wild birds, such as yellow-shouldered parrots in Venezuela in the 1990s. Parker was finally placed in a new nest on 22 December, and his adoptive mother, Tambo, started preening him straight away. A few months later, he managed to fledge. He was the only fourth chick to do so in decades of observations of wild nests in Tambopata. The team found similar success with 25 other chicks they've rescued between 2017 and 2019. A further three were successfully adopted but failed to fly the nest (as they were killed by lighting, a predator and disease). By 2019, Vigo-Trauco was feeling more confident: "I felt like playing chess – moving here and there to see what was possible." But while some moves forward can be made with wild foster-parenting, it is also beset by challenges. It is expensive work. In her three-year experiment in Tambopata, Vigo-Trauco had enough funding to pay salaries, lodging and equipment for a 20-person team. Yet such ambition "can't be easily replicated", she says. It is also hard to pull off. Rony García-Anleu is director of biological research at the Wildlife Conservation Society in Guatemala. He pioneered the adoption method in the last remaining scarlet macaw populations in Guatemala, and co-authored Vigo-Trauco's paper on fostering.   But the last time García-Anleu's team introduced a bird to a foster nest in Guatemala was in 2019. Wild fostering requires perfect timing, he says. You need to trek miles into the jungle to locate a nest with a chick in danger. Then quickly find a couple with a suitable nest that is either empty or with one chick of a similar age.  Instead, his team teach the macaws how to fly, feed and bond in a massive cage, then release them when they're ready. In 1994 in Costa Rica, macaws had also been decimated by deforestation and poaching . But a team led by conservationist Christopher Vaugh began guarding active nests, introducing education sessions in schools and installing artificial nests to improve the supply of suitable nesting sites. Their effort stabilised and recovered the population – and demonstrated, according to Vaugh, that one must address the root causes of the species' vulnerability: forest loss and poaching. Despite its flaws, however, the wild fostering technique is now informing work with other species of parrots, from Argentina to Central America, says Vigo-Trauco. Plus, since 2020 she has been testing a refinement: skipping the hand-rearing phase altogether and moving chicks from one nest to another as soon as they are born. This new approach requires more monitoring, but less intensive care for newborns – making it cheaper to run. And, in the project's second year, it has already had success: two nests, each with two chicks with large age gaps, were successfully switched up so the parents could raise two similarly aged chicks. More like this: • Nine things you probably didn't know about sharks • Pangolins: The world's most-trafficked wild animal • When trillions of creatures rise from ocean depths Vigo-Trauco believes this may open the door for fostering in places with fewer resources. "It's nice to see that our relatively healthier population allowed us to become a source of knowledge for others," says Vigo-Trauco. As for Parker, he managed to leave the nest and spread his wings. Vigo-Trauco's team saw him once again in September of 2019, now a young and confident macaw flying alongside his adoptive parents and his sibling. "It was 'normal' family," she says, "with two fledglings."  -- For essential climate news and hopeful developments to your inbox, sign up to the Future Earth newsletter, while The Essential List delivers a handpicked selection of features and insights twice a week.  For more science, technology, environment and health stories from the BBC, follow us on Facebook and Instagram Earth Animal Bird Conservation Parenting Nature & Outdoors Environment Science Features

5天前 分享 收藏 在Google上添加为首选 迭戈·阿格达斯·奥尔蒂斯 绯红金刚鹦鹉是一种标志性但数量不断下降的热带鸟类。为了改变这一物种的命运，科学家们正致力于对抗一种致命的育儿方式，这种方式让许多雏鸟注定死亡。帕克还没睁开眼，就被一只手从巢中抓走了。那是2018年11月的一个周一早晨，地点是秘鲁亚马孙雨林深处的坦博帕塔国家保护区。这只浑身无毛的雏鸟虚弱、体重不足，身长不过一根中指。他是四只绯红金刚鹦鹉兄弟姐妹中最小的那只，而这意味着他几乎注定会被饿死。站在树下的，是策划这次“绑架”的秘鲁科学家加布里埃拉·比戈-特劳科。通过二十多年对这些鸟的研究，比戈-特劳科发现，绯红金刚鹦鹉会故意饿死自己最小的雏鸟。这位来自得克萨斯农工大学的科学家发现，在多枚蛋的巢中，几乎所有的第三只和第四只雏鸟都活不下来，大约25%的第二只雏鸟也会遭遇同样的命运。这种残酷的育儿方式曾经是一种生存策略。如今，它却成了这个数量下降物种恢复的一大制约——盗猎和伐木已经使一个亚种在墨西哥和中美洲各地濒临灭绝。2017年，比戈-特劳科启动了一项极少有人尝试的救助行动，这也让她找到了那只被她命名为帕克的雏鸟。她的目标是招募野生绯红金刚鹦鹉夫妇，成为这些注定死亡雏鸟的养父母。通过说服野生鸟类承担这一任务，她希望为秘鲁这些被忽视的后代——以及更广泛的整个物种——测试一条新的生路。绯红金刚鹦鹉绝不会被错过。它们深红色的羽毛在森林的绿色中格外醒目，而早在看见它们之前，你就能听到它们的尖叫声。每只雌鸟每个繁殖季最多可产下四枚蛋，但通常只有一两只雏鸟能飞离巢穴。“父母，尤其是母亲，会把最小的那只推开，”比戈-特劳科说。她是秘鲁保护组织“金刚鹦鹉学会”的联合主任，该组织在2007年安装巢内摄像头后首次揭示了这种行为。“那只雏鸟又冷又不停地叫，当父亲回来时，他会喂母亲、喂第一只和第二只雏鸟，却任由第三只继续叫嚷。”这里没有兄弟姐妹间的欺凌，也与食物是否充足无关。那么，父母为什么忽视较小的雏鸟？比戈-特劳科认为，父母无法很好应对处于不同发育阶段的雏鸟。即使孵化时间只差四五天，也会造成巨大差异，导致雏鸟需要截然不同的喂养方式，甚至不同的巢温。她说，父母被迫做出选择。如果它们过度勉强自己去喂养所有雏鸟，就有可能非

##段落
我们能做到。对于秘鲁亚马孙地区相对健康的绯红金刚鹦鹉种群来说，幼鸟的损失影响较小。但在那些保护主义者要为每一只鸟的生存而与偷猎者和伐木者斗争的国家，维戈-特劳科说，哪怕只有几只幼鸟死亡也是一场灾难。人工饲养被遗弃的幼鸟是一种可能的解决方案。但它们可能需要1.5到3个月才能飞走。此外，圈养长大的鹦鹉存活率出了名地低：它们难以在野外觅食、识别捕食者并融入鸟群。因此，维戈-特劳科的团队转向了野生养父母的想法。2018年他们查获帕克后，维戈-特劳科的团队在野外工作站手工喂养了他三周，遵循每两小时喂一次的不间断时间表。他们还筛查了森林中的巢穴，为这只幼鸟找到合适的寄养家庭，好教它如何像野鸟一样生活。过去几十年里，圈养金刚鹦鹉的鸟类饲养者已经测试过这种技术，那里的条件可控，换巢不过意味着抱着一只幼鸟穿过走廊。它也建立在涉及其他野生鸟类的实验基础上，比如20世纪90年代委内瑞拉的黄肩鹦鹉。帕克最终于12月22日被放入一个新巢，他的养母坦博立刻开始为他理羽。几个月后，他成功离巢飞翔。在坦博帕塔数十年的野生巢穴观察中，他是第四只做到这一点的幼鸟。研究团队在2017年至2019年间救助的其他25只幼鸟身上也取得了类似成功。另有3只被成功收养，但未能飞离巢穴（因为它们分别死于闪电、捕食者和疾病）。到2019年，维戈-特劳科感到更有信心了：“我觉得自己像在下棋——这里走一步，那里走一步，看看什么是可能的。”但是，尽管野生寄养可以带来一些进展，它也面临重重挑战。这项工作成本高昂。在坦博帕塔为期三年的实验中，维戈-特劳科有足够的资金为一个20人团队支付工资、住宿和设备费用。然而，她说，这样的雄心“无法轻易复制”。这件事也很难做成。罗尼·加西亚-安莱乌是危地马拉野生动物保护协会的生物研究主任。他在危地马拉仅存的绯红金刚鹦鹉种群中率先采用了这种收养方法，并与维戈-特劳科合著了关于寄养的论文。但加西亚-安莱乌的团队上一次在危地马拉把一只鸟引入寄养巢穴还是在2019年。他说，野生寄养需要完美的时机。你需要徒步数英里深入丛林，找到一个有处于危险中的幼鸟的巢穴。然后迅速找到一对拥有合适巢穴的鸟，这个巢穴要么是空的，要么有一只年龄相近的幼鸟。相反，他的团队教那些

## 金刚鹦鹉如何在大笼子里学会飞行、觅食和建立联系，然后在准备好后放归野外。1994年，在哥斯达黎加，金刚鹦鹉也因森林砍伐和偷猎而数量锐减。但由环保主义者克里斯托弗·沃恩领导的团队开始守护活跃的巢穴，在学校开展教育活动，并安装人工巢穴以增加适宜筑巢地点的供给。他们的努力稳定并恢复了种群数量——据沃恩所说，这也证明了必须解决该物种脆弱性的根本原因：森林丧失和偷猎。然而，维戈-特劳科表示，尽管这种野生寄养技术存在缺陷，它如今正在为从阿根廷到中美洲的其他鹦鹉物种保护工作提供借鉴。此外，自2020年以来，她一直在测试一项改进方案：完全跳过人工育雏阶段，在雏鸟一出生时就将其从一个巢穴转移到另一个巢穴。这种新方法需要更多监测，但对新生雏鸟的密集照料更少——因此运营成本更低。在项目实施的第二年，这一方法已经取得了成功：两个巢穴，每个都有两只年龄差距很大的雏鸟，被成功调换，使父母能够抚养两只年龄相仿的雏鸟。更多类似内容：• 关于鲨鱼，你可能不知道的九件事 • 穿山甲：世界上被贩运最多的野生动物 • 当数万亿生物从海洋深处升起时 维戈-特劳科认为，这可能为资源较少地区的寄养工作打开大门。“很高兴看到，我们相对更健康的种群使我们能够成为其他地区的知识来源，”维戈-特劳科说。至于帕克，他成功离开了巢穴，展翅高飞。维戈-特劳科的团队在2019年9月再次见到了他，此时他已是一只年轻而自信的金刚鹦鹉，与养父母和同胞一起飞翔。“那是一个‘正常’的家庭，”她说，“有两只刚会飞的幼鸟。”——欲获取重要气候新闻和充满希望的进展，请订阅《未来地球》通讯，而《精选清单》每周两次为您送上精心挑选的特稿与洞见。更多来自BBC的科学、技术、环境和健康故事，请在Facebook和Instagram上关注我们 地球 动物 鸟类 保护 育儿 自然与户外 环境 科学 特稿

readings.title: Is Italy the new tax haven for the global rich?
body: 22 April 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google John Laurenson Italy has already been attacked by the French Government for using tax incentives to lure wealthy French and other international residents away, but with the war in the Middle East hurting the Gulf states, Italy has become an even more attractive location for the rich. Tax wasn't the main reason for leaving France, Robert insists over a café crème at Charles de Gaulle airport. It was the beauty of Italy, the bella vita  (the beautiful/good life), the art and the music. But for the Frenchman, buying a house in Rome and becoming an Italian tax resident was a very nice part of the package offered by the country, where high net worth individuals can pay a fixed annual tax on all foreign income – regardless of amount – and enjoy a series of other exemptions.  Robert, who describes himself as only "moderately wealthy", moved to Italy eight years ago after a career in computers which ended with him selling his company. Robert, not his real name, may not be among the French billionaires who have fled the French taxman for Italy, but the advantages to him are clear.   If he'd been buying a house in France, he would have had to pay what the French call frais de notaire (solicitor's fees) most of which goes to the government (much like Stamp Duty in the UK or Real Estate Transfer Taxes in the US). In Italy there's an exemption for the prima casa , the first house you buy. In France, President Macron transformed France's Impot sur la Fortune  (wealth tax) into an Impot sur la Fortune Immobilière  (real estate wealth tax) so stock market investments, for example, are no longer affected but "if you have ten million dollars' worth of property, this tax is very painful indeed," says Robert. Again, there's nothing like that in Italy.  In France you also have to pay a property tax ( taxe foncière or land tax). "We don't have that here for the prima casa (first home)," says Robert, although he notes "there is a high charge for refuse collection". The best thing as far as he is concerned is that there is no inheritance tax on property you own in Italy up to €1 million ($1.1 million) and it's only 4% beyond that threshold. In France the tax-free limit is much lower – €100,000 ($110,000) – and beyond that it's a sliding scale up to a top rate of 45%. But it's for the seriously rich that Italy starts to look like a fiscal paradise. "I have friends who have moved here for tax reasons and others who are thinking about it," Robert tells me. "For people who really pay a lot of tax, Italy is very attractive because of it's "flat tax". In Italy, the taxman fixes an upper limit of tax that can be levied on income. However much you earn, you never pay more than that. The upper limit is now €300,000 ($353,000). Although not long ago it was €100,000 before rising to €200,000. If you're paying a million euros of income tax a year in France, Italy is very tempting. As for US citizens, Americans are always taxable on worldwide income, so moving to Italy would not help their tax bill. Even at €300,000, Italy's flat tax is still low for anyone making over €1m per year compared to anywhere else in Europe – Peter Ferrigno Robert tells me that he has two rich French friends who have moved to Italy in the past few months, but they came from the UK. They were both working in finance in the City of London and were keen to move to a place where the fiscal regime was as sympathetic to them as the one Britain had before it changed the rules for wealthy foreign residents.  "Even at €300,000, Italy's flat tax is still low for anyone making over €1m per year compared to anywhere else in Europe. And it means you get tax certainty and clarity, within the heart of Europe, rather than having to go a long way," says Peter Ferrigno, director of tax services at wealth migration specialists Henley & Partners. "We have meetings with people every week who would like to leave France," says Paris-based tax lawyer Jerome Barre. "They are unhappy about the tax situation now and they are worried that it will become harsher in the future. People are not confident with the political climate. Taxes are changing a lot, almost every year. People are frightened that after the election of the new president in 2027, things could become harder than today," he says. At this stage though it's more "questions from entrepreneurs and wealthy people who are wondering if they would like to move or not move rather than people actually moving," Jerome Barre explains. "Relocation requires full commitment and careful structuring," he stresses. He adds that for business-owners  " they need to change the seat of the company. They are subject in France to an exit tax." If many wealthy French people are at the "thinking-about-moving" stage, the question is being felt even more acutely in the United Arab Emirates. It's inevitable that many people will reconsider UAE – Peter Ferrigno But giving up on Dubai's zero-tax regime will be very difficult for many. "When you are in a country where you do not pay any tax, it's very difficult to come back to a country where you have to pay a lot. Especially for those used to spending a lot of money. The net in your pocket is very different, says Barre. And, he adds, people who have grown used to the zero-tax life "are not used to administrative formalities anymore – tax returns, documents – so it's not easy." More like this: • Dubai's tourism industry reels from 'brutal' impact of war • Why more Americans are now moving to Ireland • Is New York's cannabis business really flying high? "It's inevitable that many people will reconsider UAE," says Henley & Partners' Peter Ferrigno. "But I think it's far too early for people to wholesale uproot their life when it involves work, family, etc. The vast majority of people in the UAE are still regular people doing regular jobs, even most of the millionaires are millionaires because they are doing well paid jobs rather than being asset owners. If the war is relatively short, they will remain. If it drags on, then people will inevitably look elsewhere, or relocate the family and work remotely until it's safer. If you're in the UAE for work, there aren't likely to be that many equivalent roles in Italy," he says. However, it is likely that the war in the Middle East will dissuade many rich Europeans who would have otherwise moved there from re-locating to the UAE. Last year, Dubai was the number one destination by far for migrating millionaires, according to Henley & Partners. That number is bound to tumble in 2026, and with its attractive offer for the very wealthy, as well as its reputation for  la dolce vita  of course, it may well be Italy that benefits. -- For global insights and expert analysis for the boardroom and beyond, sign up to the  World of Business newsletter , while  The Essential List  delivers a handpicked selection of features and insights.  For more on business and beyond, follow us on  LinkedIn . 2026年4月22日 分享 保存 在Google上添加为首选 约翰·劳伦森 意大利已经因利用税收优惠吸引富有的法国人和其他国际居民而遭到法国政府的抨击，但随着中东战争对海湾国家造成冲击，意大利对富人来说变得更具吸引力。罗伯特在戴高乐机场喝着一杯咖啡奶油时坚称，税收并非他离开法国的主要原因。真正的原因是意大利的美丽、美好的生活、艺术和音乐。但对这位法国人来说，在罗马买房并成为意大利税务居民，是这个国家所提供的一揽子方案中非常令人满意的一部分——在意大利，高净值个人可以就所有海外收入缴纳固定的年度税额，无论金额多少，并享受一系列其他豁免。罗伯特自称只是“中等富裕”，八年前在结束计算机行业的职业生涯并出售了自己的公司后移居意大利。罗伯特（化名）或许不在那些为逃避法国税务而逃往意大利的法国亿万富翁之列，但对他来说，好处是显而易见的。如果他是在法国买房，就必须支付法国人所说的“公证费”，其中大部分归政府所有（类似于英国的印花税或美国的房地产转让税）。而在意大利，首次购房享有豁免。在法国，马克龙总统将法国的“财富税”转变为“房地产财富税”，因此股票市场投资等不再受影响，但罗伯特说，“如果你拥有价值一千万美元的房产，这项税确实非常沉重。”而在意大利，完全没有这样的税。在法国，你还必须缴纳房产税（土地税）。“我们这里对首套住房没有这项税，”罗伯特说，不过他指出“垃圾收集费用很高”。就他而言，最好的一点是，你在意大利拥有的房产价值不超过100万欧元（约110万美元）时无需缴纳遗产税，超过该门槛也仅需缴纳4%。而在法国，免税上限要低得多——仅为10万欧元（约11万美元）——超过部分则按累进税率征收，最高可达45%。但正是对真正的富豪而言，意大利才开始看起来像是一个税收天堂。“我有朋友因税收原因搬到了这里，还有一些人正在考虑，”罗伯特告诉我。“对于真正缴纳大量税款的人来说，意大利非常有吸引力，因为它有‘单一税’。在意大利，税务部门对可征收的收入设定了上限。无论你赚多少，你缴纳的税款都不会超过这个上限。目前的上限是30万欧元（约35.3万美元）。尽管

##段落
不久前还是10万欧元，后来涨到20万欧元。如果你在法国每年缴纳100万欧元的所得税，意大利就非常有吸引力了。至于美国公民，美国人始终需要就全球收入纳税，所以搬到意大利并不会减轻他们的税负。即便税率定在30万欧元，对于年收入超过100万欧元的人来说，意大利的单一税率与欧洲其他地方相比仍然很低——彼得·费里尼奥告诉我，他有两位富裕的法国朋友在过去几个月搬到了意大利，但他们是从英国搬过去的。这两人此前都在伦敦金融城从事金融工作，迫切希望搬到一个财税制度对他们友善的地方，就像英国在修改针对富裕外国居民的规则之前那样。

##段落
“即便税率定在30万欧元，对于年收入超过100万欧元的人来说，意大利的单一税率与欧洲其他地方相比仍然很低。而且这意味着你可以在欧洲腹地获得税收的确定性和清晰度，而不必远走他乡，”财富移民专业机构Henley & Partners的税务服务总监彼得·费里尼奥表示。“我们每周都会与想要离开法国的人会面，”巴黎税务律师杰罗姆·巴雷说。“他们对当前的税收状况不满，担心未来会变得更加严苛。人们对政治气候缺乏信心。税收变化很大，几乎每年都在变。人们害怕2027年新总统当选后，情况会比现在更糟，”他说。不过，巴雷解释说，现阶段更多的是“企业家和富裕人士在思考自己要不要搬走，而不是真的已经搬走了”。“搬迁需要全身心的投入和精心的规划，”他强调。他还补充说，对于企业主而言，“他们需要更换公司的注册地。在法国，他们需要缴纳退出税。”

##段落
如果说许多富裕的法国人还处于“考虑搬迁”的阶段，那么在阿联酋，这个问题感受得更为迫切。许多人重新考虑阿联酋是不可避免的——彼得·费里尼奥。但对许多人来说，放弃迪拜的零税制将非常困难。“当你身处一个完全不缴税的国家，再回到一个需要缴纳大量税款的国家，是非常困难的。尤其是那些习惯了高消费的人。到手收入差别非常大，”巴雷说。他还补充道，那些已经习惯了零税生活的人“不再习惯行政手续——纳税申报、文件——所以并不容易。”更多类似内容：• 迪拜旅游业遭受战争“残酷”冲击 • 为什么越来越多美国人移居爱尔兰 • 纽约的大麻生意真的在起飞吗

## 嗯？“很多人重新考虑阿联酋，这是不可避免的，”Henley & Partners的彼得·费里尼奥表示。“但我认为，现在就让人彻底连根拔起、放弃工作、家庭等一切，还为时过早。阿联酋的绝大多数人仍然是做着普通工作的普通人，即便是大多数百万富翁，他们之所以是百万富翁，也是因为从事高薪工作，而非拥有资产。如果战争相对短暂，他们会留下来。如果战争拖下去，人们必然会另寻他处，或者把家人安置到别处、自己远程工作，直到局势更安全。如果你在阿联酋是为了工作，意大利恐怕不会有那么多对等的职位，”他说。然而，中东战争很可能会让许多原本会迁往那里的富裕欧洲人打消移居阿联酋的念头。根据Henley & Partners的数据，去年迪拜是迄今为止迁移百万富翁的首选目的地。这一数字在2026年势必大幅下滑，而凭借其对超级富豪的吸引力，当然还有“甜蜜生活”的声誉，受益的很可能是意大利。——欲获取面向董事会及更高层面的全球洞察与专家分析，请订阅《商业世界》通讯，而《精选清单》则为您呈上精心挑选的专题与洞察。欲了解更多商业及更多领域的内容，请在领英上关注我们。商业 国际商业 专题 《商业世界》

readings.title: Why we should all be partying more
body: Explain It to Me Why we should all be partying more The historical case for partying it up, explained. by Jonquilyn Hill Sep 20, 2026, 11:00 AM UTC Gift A.H. Fish/Condé Nast via Getty Images Jonquilyn Hill is the host of Explain It to Me , your hotline for all your unanswered questions. She joined Vox in 2022 as a senior producer and then as host of The Weeds , Vox’s policy podcast. We are in the midst of a loneliness epidemic: More than half of Americans say they feel isolated , and we’re getting together less and less. In 2023, only about 4 percent of adults said they went to a party on a weekend or holiday. According to Imogen Willetts , a party historian and author of the book Up All Night: A History of Going Out , this moment is an outlier. “For most of human history, the experiences that we associate with nightlife — drinking, dancing, music, hedonism — those experiences were simply part of religion because religion was so all-encompassing,” she told Vox. If parties are so ingrained in humankind, then, what are we missing when we don’t get out the door on a Friday night anymore? And what lessons can we learn from the turnups of yore? We get into all of that and more — including how to throw a great party and how to be a good guest — on the latest episode Explain It to Me , Vox’s weekly call-in podcast. Below is an excerpt of my conversation with Willetts, edited for length and clarity. You can listen to the full episode on Apple Podcasts , Spotify , or wherever you get your podcasts. If you’d like to submit a question, send an email to askvox@vox.com or call 1-800-618-8545. Can you talk about the role religion played in early nightlife? Because I think we often think of religion and partying as two separate things, but that was not the case for all of history, was it? [Religion] contained people’s hedonistic instinct. There was nothing really outside of it. And so there’s even evidence, which I love thinking about this, that the churchgoing experience in medieval England was actually quite rowdy and quite raucous. On feast days there would be drinking, there would be dancing. And there’s one theory that wooden pews were introduced in Wells Cathedral in England to subdue the dancing because it was so raucous. And so in some sense, it takes us a while to get to nightlife because we sort of didn’t need it for a very long time. Religion contained hedonism quite comfortably within it. Seventeenth-century Japan, I would say, is the beginning of modern nightlife because we have these commercial party scenes, nightlife environments, which have nothing to do with religion, “Whether it’s at a sports match or a concert stadium, and even within religion — that is collective effervescence.” Crucially, they’re also separate from court. Another part of party scenes is court spectacle — think Louis XIV and Versailles and all of that stuff that was contained within these monarchical structures. So the first real nightlife destination is Yoshiwara, which was built on the outskirts of Edo, which is now Tokyo. The idea of church being a place to party is so interesting. I do get the same feeling I get at church when I’m on the dance floor and I hear Kaytranada. I can imagine how these religious experiences allowed people to access that feeling of release through music and through dance. An expression that I came across when researching the book that I think really wonderfully kind of captures the essence of nightlife and partying is this term coined by the sociologist Émile Durkheim in 1912, which is “collective effervescence.” That’s the feeling that we experience during peak communal experiences. Whether it’s at a sports match or a concert stadium, and even within religion — that is collective effervescence. That is the same sensation, that surge of euphoria that people feel on dance floors. I think parties and nightlife are such an important way to access this very important human feeling, particularly in societies that are increasingly atheist or increasingly secular. We need nightlife to have these communal euphoric experiences and feel part of something bigger than ourselves. You’ve written about how, yes, parties are fun, but they’re also at the epicenter of some pretty important cultural and societal shifts. I think nightlife is very uniquely poised to allow for experimentation and innovation and transgression. Also, in a very practical way, if you’re part of the abstract expressionist scene of mid-century New York or something, you need somewhere to meet and talk to people and figure out how you’re going to sell your work that’s like nothing people have ever seen before. These social spaces play a really, really important role in culture. The abstract expressionist artists were hanging out in the Cedar Tavern, and then you have things like the Viennese Secession Movement and Cabaret Fledermaus was part of that meeting space. Similarly, you get things like dance and music that’s very much created for dance floors, for clubbing, for nightlife: the can-can and then disco and then techno. Nightlife has been so crucial to the propulsion of culture. A lot of this is happening in the club, but what about parties happening in private homes ? One of the great examples of people opening up their homes in a sense of turning the home into a club was turn-of-the-century New Orleans. On Saturday nights, people would host fish fries: Basically, when you would open up your home to the public, you would charge entry at the door. Once inside, people were treated to this amazing spread of food, drink, and there would be bands that would perform. It was often a way for households who were struggling with rent payments to earn some extra cash. It happened again in Harlem in the 1920s. Langston Hughes writes about the Saturday night rent parties , where people’s apartments would be opened up in the exact same way. He said they were more interesting than anything that was going on in the cabarets and the clubs. He was going to those as often as he could and collecting the invitations for them. People would write their address on business cards, leave them in different shops and pubs and hairdressers or whatever, and then you would pick them up and then go to the party. Langston Hughes collected them, and they now are randomly in a Yale archive of all places. As you think of parties over the centuries, are there elements that all the best parties have in common? At their very core essence, you need good music, you need good lighting, and I think also you need to create this atmosphere where the sense that anything can happen. What you want is for the people that are at your party to feel like they can behave differently or do something a little bit wild. I think that there’s something very satisfying in experiencing a domestic world upturned. I think seeing the kitchen become a gloomy cocktail bar, the living room becoming a dance floor — there’s something very satisfying in experiencing that. It goes back to what the heart of nightlife culture or party culture is all about. We want to shed our daily lives. You want that sense of slight disorder that makes people feel alive. 解释给我听：为什么我们都应该多参加派对。为狂欢作乐的历史依据，详解。作者：琼奎琳·希尔 2026年9月20日，上午11:00 UTC。礼物。A.H. 菲什/康泰纳仕，经由盖蒂图片社。琼奎琳·希尔是《解释给我听》的主持人，这是你所有未解问题的热线。她于2022年加入Vox，担任高级制作人，随后担任Vox政策播客《杂草》的主持人。我们正身处一场孤独流行病之中：超过一半的美国人说他们感到孤立，而我们聚在一起的次数越来越少。2023年，只有约4%的成年人表示，他们曾在周末或假日参加派对。根据派对历史学家、《彻夜不眠：外出史》一书作者伊莫金·威莱茨的说法，当下这一刻是一个异数。她对Vox说：“在人类历史的大部分时间里，我们与夜生活联系在一起的体验——饮酒、跳舞、音乐、享乐主义——那些体验只是宗教的一部分，因为宗教无所不包。”那么，如果派对对人类社会如此根深蒂固，当我们不再在周五晚上出门时，我们到底错过了什么？我们又能从往昔的狂欢中吸取什么教训？我们会在最新一集《解释给我听》——Vox的每周来电播客——中讨论这一切以及更多内容，包括如何举办一场精彩的派对，以及如何做一个好客人。以下是我与威莱茨对话的节选，为长度和清晰度作了编辑。你可以在Apple Podcasts、Spotify或任何你收听播客的地方收听完整一集。如果你想提交问题，请发送电子邮件至askvox@vox.com，或致电1-800-618-8545。

##段落
你能谈谈宗教在早期夜生活中扮演的角色吗？因为我觉得我们常把宗教和派对视为两件分开的事，但在整个历史中并非如此，对吧？

##段落
[宗教]容纳了人们的享乐本能。它之外几乎没有什么东西。所以甚至有证据表明——我很喜欢思考这一点——中世纪英格兰去教堂的经历其实相当喧闹、相当嘈杂。在节庆日会有饮酒，会有跳舞。有一种理论认为，英格兰韦尔斯大教堂引入木制长椅，是为了压制跳舞，因为场面太喧闹了。所以在某种意义上，我们花了很长时间才走到夜生活，因为我们在很长一段时间里 sort of 并不需要它。宗教相当舒适地把享乐主义容纳在其中。我会说，17世纪的日本是现代夜生活的开端，因为我们有了这些商业派对场景、夜生活环境，它们与宗教毫无关系，

场景是宫廷奇观——想想路易十四和凡尔赛宫，以及所有这些君主制结构内所包含的东西。所以第一个真正的夜生活目的地是吉原，它建在江户（也就是现在的东京）的郊外。教堂作为派对场所的想法太有趣了。当我在舞池里听到Kaytranada时，我确实会有和在教堂里一样的感觉。我可以想象这些宗教体验如何让人们通过音乐和舞蹈获得那种释放感。在研究这本书时，我遇到了一个表达，我认为它非常精彩地捕捉到了夜生活和派对的本质，这是社会学家埃米尔·涂尔干在1912年创造的一个术语——“集体欢腾”。那就是我们在巅峰 communal 体验中所感受到的感觉。无论是在体育比赛还是演唱会体育场，甚至在宗教中——那就是集体欢腾。那是同样的感觉，那种人们在舞池上感受到的兴奋涌动。我认为派对和夜生活是获得这种非常重要的人类感觉的重要方式，尤其是在越来越无神论或越来越世俗的社会中。我们需要夜生活来拥有这些 communal 的狂喜体验，并感到自己属于比自身更宏大的事物。你写过，是的，派对很有趣，但它们也处于一些相当重要的文化和社会转变的中心。我认为夜生活非常独特地适合允许实验、创新和越界。而且，以一种非常实际的方式，如果你是20世纪中期纽约抽象表现主义场景的一部分，你需要一个地方来见面、交谈，并弄清楚如何出售你的作品，这些作品是人们从未见过的。这些社交空间在文化中扮演着非常非常重要的角色。抽象表现主义艺术家们在Cedar Tavern聚会，然后还有像维也纳分离派运动这样的东西，Cabaret Fledermaus是那个聚会空间的一部分。同样，你会看到为舞池、为俱乐部、为夜生活而创作的舞蹈和音乐：康康舞，然后是迪斯科，然后是 techno。夜生活对文化的推进至关重要。很多这些都发生在俱乐部里，但私人家中举办的派对呢？人们开放自己的家，在某种意义上把家变成俱乐部的一个伟大例子是世纪之交的新奥尔良。在周六晚上，人们会举办炸鱼宴：基本上，当你向公众开放你的家时，你会在门口收取入场费。一旦进去，人们会享受到令人惊叹的食物、饮料，还会有b

##那些能表演的乐队。这往往是那些为租金发愁的家庭赚点外快的方式。1920年代在哈莱姆又出现了同样的情况。兰斯顿·休斯写到过周六晚上的“租金派对”，人们的公寓以完全相同的方式对外开放。他说这些派对比卡巴莱和俱乐部里发生的任何事情都有趣。他尽可能频繁地去参加，并收集派对的邀请函。人们会把地址写在名片上，留在不同的商店、酒吧、理发店之类的地方，然后你拿到名片就可以去参加派对。兰斯顿·休斯把这些名片收集了起来，如今它们竟然被存放在耶鲁大学的档案馆里。当你回顾几个世纪以来的派对，所有最好的派对是否有共同之处？就其核心本质而言，你需要好的音乐，你需要好的灯光，我认为你还需要营造出这样一种氛围——让人感觉一切皆有可能。你想要的是让来参加派对的人觉得自己可以表现得不一样，或者做点有点疯狂的事。我觉得体验一个被颠覆的居家世界，有一种非常令人满足的感觉。看着厨房变成一间昏暗的鸡尾酒吧，客厅变成舞池——体验这些让人非常满足。这要追溯到夜生活文化或派对文化的核心究竟是什么。我们想要摆脱日常生活。你想要那种轻微的失序感，让人们觉得自己是活着的。查看更多：解释给我听 生活播客 用最新的Vox填字游戏让大脑休息一下 不想要孩子的奇怪悲伤 阻止卡玛拉2028的静默运动正在壮大 一部关于加沙的以色列纪录片正在席卷全球——而以色列人怒不可遏 播客 为什么特朗普的拉丁裔选民正在离他而去 播客 电子邮件（必填） 注册 提交你的电子邮件即表示你同意我们的条款和隐私声明。本网站受reCAPTCHA保护，谷歌隐私政策和服务条款适用。广告商内容来自 这是原生广告的标题

readings.title: How the world realised whales are singing
body: 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Jocelyn Timperley A series of discoveries in the 1950s, 60s and 70s overturned everything we knew about whales, propelling them into human culture as the charismatic animals we know today. It was 1952 and the height of the Cold War. US sonar engineer Frank Watlington was stationed off the coast of Bermuda, listening in the depths for Soviet submarines and seismic activity. Watlington was using an early kind of hydrophone: long cables with a microphone at the end that he would sink into the ocean. It's not known what military operations he may have detected, but he did begin to pick up something else.  The mournful, disconcerting sounds would go on sometimes for hours. Watlington was fascinated. He couldn't be sure, but he began to think they were being made by humpback whales. It turned out he was right. Watlington and others' incredible early recordings of humpback communication would go on to transform our view of whales forever. When these were featured on the iconic 1970 album Songs of the Humpback Whale, they introduced the otherworldly sounds of whale song to a world that previously barely knew it existed. Whale song exploded into popular culture, becoming the soundtrack to the emerging Save the Whales movement that would eventually turn around the declining fortunes of humpbacks. (Scroll down to listen to a clip from the album). Watlington began sharing his recordings with locals and researchers, and in 1967 he met acoustic biologists Katy and Roger Payne, who had travelled to Bermuda. He played them the recordings in the engine room of his research vessel – a wooden ex-minesweeper from World War Two – while the generator roared in the background. "What I heard under impossibly awful conditions of listening was the most extraordinary, amazing acoustic performance I'd ever heard from any animal, and have ever heard from any animal since," Roger, who died in 2023, told the BBC's The Documentary podcast in 2020 .  The couple were amazed by the beautiful, incredibly variable sounds. "They were, as we learned later, the sounds of just one animal," Katy told NPR in 2015 . "Just one animal." Watlington lent them a recording, which Katy, Roger and their collaborators (conservationist Scott McVay, mathematician Hella McVay and researcher Eleanora D'Arms) began working to decipher. The oldest whale recording There are scattered historic accounts from sailors and whalers describing humpback whale song, but most had faded into obscurity by the early 20th Century. In 2026, an even older 1949 recording of humpback whales was discovered. The scientists who recorded it near Bermuda didn't know what it was at the time, though, and simply labelled it "fish noises". They realised that the sounds were being repeated in long, predictable patterns. "You couldn't listen to it 100 times as I have done without realising that slowly," Roger told the BBC in 2020. "When an animal makes a sound which is rhythmic and repeats itself, it is defined as being singing." Sometimes the songs would go on for up to half an hour, only to be repeated again and again.  People generally knew at the time that whales produced sounds, says Nan Hauser, a whale researcher and director of the Center for Cetacean Research and Conservation in the Cook Islands. But realising this was song was "an enormous conceptual leap… from an animal making noises to an animal producing an extraordinarily elaborate, organised acoustic display".  Roger, an environmentalist dedicated to saving what he would refer to as the "wild world", quickly realised he had more in his hands than a scientific discovery.  He began playing the tracks to anyone who would listen: at anti-whaling protests, at conferences, at dinner parties. "He was like a little kid with a new toy that everybody had to listen to," says Iain Kerr, chief executive of Ocean Alliance, a US-based non-profit that Roger Payne went on to found. "And really what a catalyst it was… to suddenly go, 'Oh my god, these are sort of singer-poets, composers'." Song is quite an unusual behaviour in the natural world, and its new association with whales resonated with people, says Andy Rogan, a marine mammal biologist and science and conservation director at Ocean Alliance. Apart from humans, it was really just birds that were thought to sing, he says. "On one level it's not necessarily that different from another animal behaviour… [But] what's the purpose of going for half an hour? For an animal that takes up a lot of mental capacity." In 1970, Roger, Katy and Watlington released Songs of the Humpback Whale, an album containing five recordings of humpback whales, chosen specifically for their beauty and power to move humans.  The album was a resounding success, rapidly bringing the haunting sounds of humpbacks to millions of people. It sold more than 125,000 copies – making it the biggest selling nature album in history – and an extract was sent to all 10.5 million National Geographic subscribers, the largest single pressing in recording history. "No one had really heard anything like this before," says Kerr. Roger used the album to drum up support for whale protection, sending out copies to everyone from the Beatles to Bob Dylan. Singers Judy Collins and Kate Bush featured whale song in their albums. Extracts were used in a 1986 film Star Trek film , in a time travel plot about rescuing humpback whales from extinction. In 1977, an excerpt was even launched into space, on the Voyager 1 Golden Record phonograph . Exposure to the sounds of large whales before 1970 was rare, says Max Bridge, an environmental historian at Harvard University in the US who wrote a recent paper on the history of humpback whale song . "In popular movies and cartoons in the 1960s, fictional large whales are usually either silent or make beastly growling, grunting sounds." The album's release formed part of a wider shift in the public's perception of whales at the time, says Rogan. Whales were previously often seen as something to fear, as in stories like Moby Dick , or as a commodity, he says. "Whales are [now] part of that upper echelon of charismatic wildlife that we all grow up with… I don't think that was the case before these songs came out."  Hunted for centuries for everything from oil used for lighting and soap to the ambergris used in perfumes , by the early 1970s, several whale species were on the brink of extinction. This included humpbacks : less than 5% of their pre-whaling numbers remained. Why do whales sing? Even today, it's not known exactly why humpback whales sing. Since it's mainly males that sing, it's often thought to be related to mating , such as attracting females or warding off competing males. But it could be far more complicated. Some scientists suggest it could be a form of long-range communication and echolocation , with animals changing the pitch to help create maps of their underwater worlds. "A singer may be advertising something about himself," says Hauser. "There may be social functions that we haven't recognised yet." Together with mid-1970s images of whales being harpooned taken by a newly-formed Greenpeace, Songs of the Humpback Whales helped to galvanised a fledgling anti-whaling movement . "[It] allowed ordinary people to hear whales in their own homes," says Hauser. "You didn't need to be a scientist to be moved by it." Amidst rising pressure, in 1972, the US Congress passed the Marine Mammal Protection Act , and in 1982 a legally binding global moratorium on commercial whaling was passed, followed by a full ban in 1985-86. Populations of some whales began to increase, and humpbacks in particular have since seen a remarkable recovery . In some places, they are now even being seen in super-groups of hundreds at a time. The discovery of whale song formed part of a wider revolution in environmentalism and understanding of animal intelligence occurring at the time. Rachel Carson had published Silent Spring in 1962, examining the environmental impact of synthetic pesticides. The first Earth Day in 1970 mobilised some 20 million people, while scientists like Jane Goodall and Dian Fossey were busy transforming our understanding of other intelligent primates. Whale song started being seen as a symbol of a broader ecological crises, even as "mournful pleas on the part of the natural world", says Bridge. By the late 1970s, though, US popular culture became more cynical towards symbols of earnest environmentalism like whales or their song, they add, then in the 1980s it was adopted as a key sound of New Age music. Even today it is still largely viewed as a kind of relaxant for the stresses of white-collar life, adds Bridge. At the same time, whale song discovery helped kickstart modern whale biology in the previously poorly studied animals, says Rogan. Katy discovered that all males in one area will sing roughly the same song – and that this song evolves over time. We now know these songs can also spread from population to population across enormous distances, sometimes rapidly replacing a previous local favourite. "We're watching culture move through an ocean," says Hauser. And while humpbacks have the most complex known song among whales (it even shows some hallmarks of human language ), the sounds of other whales have also astonished researchers. Sperm whales, for example, which converse in Morse code-like sequences of clicks known as codas , are now known to have regional dialects , while males also make separate slower, deeper and enormously loud clicks . And the immense calls of the blue whale , too low for the human ear to pick up, can travel up to 1,000 miles (1,600km ). Some researchers are even trying to converse with whales and decipher what they are saying . In later life, Roger became involved in this effort . There are now thousands of recordings of whale sounds and other nature sounds pleasing to the human ear. Still, Kerr argues, none quite have the "harmony or the sort of enchanting nature" of those '70s tracks. "There's a wonderful sort of aesthetic to it, this sort of crackling, haunting voice from the deep." Perhaps the period just happened to feature especially beautiful humpback whale song, says Alyssa Wile, who is in charge of digitising and archiving Ocean Alliance's vast collection archive of marine mammal sounds  from the 1950s to 1990s, including many recorded by Katy and Roger. More like this: • Humpback whales are forming super-groups • The human-like 'alphabet' of whales • The sounds revealing the secrets of world's most elusive whales Wile still remembers listening to Songs of the Humpback Whale for the first time as a child. "It's extraordinary, and every time I listen to it, I do get the chills." Today, whales compete within a very different soundscape of anthropogenic noise , making protecting older recordings incredibly important, she says. "These recordings preserve a particular moment in space and time as well as particular individuals," she says. "We can track those changes over time, how whales are communicating differently, how the soundscape itself is different." Whales still face many threats, from ship strikes and entanglement in nets to ongoing whaling in some countries to noise pollution and warming seas . Today, one in four whale species is threatened with extinction, up from one in seven in 1991.  Still, Songs of the Humpback Whale "was unquestionably one of the great catalysts" towards protecting whales, says Hauser. "Most people would never see a living humpback whale, but suddenly they could put a record on and hear one," she says. "Suddenly the conversation wasn't simply, 'How many whales remain?'. It became 'What kind of beings are we killing?'" * Jocelyn Timperley is a senior journalist for the BBC's science features team.   -- For essential climate news and hopeful developments to your inbox, sign up to the Future Earth newsletter, while The Essential List delivers a handpicked selection of features and insights twice a week.   For more science, technology, environment and health stories from the BBC, follow us on Facebook and Instagram .  Earth Earth Shots Whale Marine life Wildlife History Features

##段落
3天前 分享 收藏 在Google上添加为首选来源 乔斯林·廷珀利 20世纪50年代、60年代和70年代的一系列发现彻底颠覆了我们对鲸鱼的认知，将鲸鱼推入人类文化，成为我们今天所熟知的那种魅力非凡的动物。那是1952年，冷战正值高峰。美国声呐工程师弗兰克·沃特灵顿驻扎在百慕大沿海，在深海中监听苏联潜艇和地震活动。沃特灵顿使用的是一种早期的水听器：长长的电缆末端装着一个麦克风，他将麦克风沉入海中。他可能探测到了什么军事行动，这已无从得知，但他确实开始捕捉到了别的东西。

##段落
那些哀伤而令人不安的声音有时会持续数小时之久。沃特灵顿为之着迷。他无法确定，但他开始认为这些声音是座头鲸发出的。事实证明他是对的。沃特灵顿和其他人早期录制的座头鲸交流录音令人惊叹，这些录音永远地改变了我们对鲸鱼的看法。当这些录音被收录进1970年那张标志性的专辑《座头鲸之歌》时，它们将鲸歌那超凡脱俗的声音介绍给了一个此前几乎不知道其存在的世界。鲸歌迅速引爆流行文化，成为新兴的“拯救鲸鱼”运动的配乐，这场运动最终扭转了座头鲸数量不断下降的命运。（向下滚动可收听专辑片段）。沃特灵顿开始与当地人和研究人员分享他的录音，1967年，他遇到了专程前往百慕大的声学生物学家凯蒂·佩恩和罗杰·佩恩。他在自己研究船的引擎舱里为他们播放了这些录音——那是一艘二战时期改装过的木制扫雷舰——背景中发电机轰鸣作响。“在极其糟糕的收听条件下，我听到的是我从任何动物身上听到过的最非凡、最惊人的声学表演，此后也再未从任何动物身上听到过，”罗杰在2020年对BBC的《纪录片》播客说道。罗杰于2023年去世。

##段落
这对夫妇被这些美妙且变化无穷的声音深深震撼。“后来我们才知道，那只是一头动物发出的声音，”凯蒂在2015年对NPR说。“仅仅一头动物。”沃特灵顿借给他们一段录音，凯蒂、罗杰及其合作者（环保主义者斯科特·麦克维、数学家海拉·麦克维和研究员埃莱奥诺拉·达姆斯）开始着手破译。

##段落
最古老的鲸鱼录音 历史上有零散的水手和捕鲸者的记载描述过座头鲸的歌声，但到20世纪初，大多数记载已湮没无闻。2026年，一段更早的1949年座头鲸录音被发现。然而，当时在百慕大附近录制这段录音的科学家并不知道那是什么，只是简单地标注为“鱼类噪音”。他们意识到这些声音在被重复

##段落
它们以悠长、可预测的模式重复着。“你若像我一样听过100遍，就不可能不慢慢意识到这一点，”罗杰在2020年接受BBC采访时说。“当动物发出有节奏、不断重复的声音时，这就可以被定义为歌唱。”有时这些歌声会持续长达半个小时，然后一遍又一遍地重复。库克群岛鲸类研究与保护中心的研究员兼主任南·豪泽说，当时人们普遍知道鲸鱼会发出声音。但意识到这是歌声，是“一个巨大的概念飞跃……从动物发出噪音，到动物呈现出极其精巧、有组织的声学表演”。罗杰是一位致力于拯救他所谓的“野性世界”的环保主义者，他很快意识到自己手中的东西远不止一项科学发现。他开始把录音放给任何愿意听的人：反捕鲸抗议现场、会议、晚宴。“他就像个拿着新玩具的小孩，非要所有人都来听，”海洋联盟首席执行官伊恩·克尔说。罗杰·佩恩后来创立了这家总部位于美国的非营利组织。“而它真的是多么强大的催化剂……让人突然惊叹，‘天哪，这些简直就是歌手兼诗人、作曲家’。”海洋哺乳动物生物学家、海洋联盟科学与保护主任安迪·罗根说，歌唱在自然界中是相当不寻常的行为，而它 newly 与鲸鱼联系在一起，引发了人们的共鸣。他说，除了人类之外，真正被认为会歌唱的其实只有鸟类。“从某个层面说，这未必与其他动物行为有多大不同……（但）持续半个小时的目的究竟是什么？对一种动物来说，这要占用大量心智能力。”1970年，罗杰、凯蒂和沃特林顿发行了《座头鲸之歌》，这张专辑收录了五段座头鲸录音，是特意因其美感和打动人心的力量而挑选的。这张专辑获得了巨大成功，迅速将座头鲸那萦绕人心的声音带给数百万人。它售出超过12.5万张——成为历史上销量最高的自然专辑——其中一段节选还被寄给了《国家地理》全部1050万名订阅者，这是录音史上规模最大的一次单次压制发行。“此前没有人真正听过这样的东西，”克尔说。罗杰利用这张专辑为鲸鱼保护争取支持，把拷贝寄给从披头士到鲍勃·迪伦的各方人士。歌手朱迪·柯林斯和凯特·布什也在自己的专辑中加入了鲸歌。1986年的一部《星际迷航》电影采用了其中节选，剧情围绕时间旅行展开，讲述从灭绝中拯救座头鲸。1977年，一段节选甚至被送入太空，搭载在“旅行者1号”的金唱片留声机上。在19

##段落
美国哈佛大学环境历史学家马克斯·布里奇最近发表了一篇关于座头鲸歌声历史的论文，他说，70年代的这种情况很罕见。“在20世纪60年代的流行电影和卡通片中，虚构的大型鲸鱼通常要么沉默不语，要么发出野兽般的咆哮和咕噜声。”罗根说，这张专辑的发行是当时公众对鲸鱼看法发生更广泛转变的一部分。他说，以前鲸鱼经常被视为可怕的东西，就像《白鲸记》等故事中那样，或者被视为商品。“（现在）鲸鱼是我们从小就熟悉的那些魅力非凡的野生动物中的上层群体……我认为在这些歌声出现之前，情况并非如此。”

##段落
几个世纪以来，从用于照明和肥皂的鲸油，到用于香水的龙涎香，鲸鱼一直遭到捕猎。到20世纪70年代初，几种鲸鱼濒临灭绝。其中包括座头鲸：其数量不到捕鲸前数量的5%。鲸鱼为什么唱歌？即使在今天，人们仍不完全清楚座头鲸为何唱歌。由于唱歌的主要是雄性，人们通常认为这与交配有关，比如吸引雌性或击退竞争的雄性。但原因可能远比这复杂。一些科学家认为，这可能是一种远距离交流和回声定位的方式，动物通过改变音高来帮助绘制其水下世界的地图。豪泽说：“歌手可能是在宣传自己的一些信息。可能还有一些我们尚未认识到的社会功能。”

##段落
结合20世纪70年代中期新成立绿色和平组织拍摄的鲸鱼被鱼叉捕杀的画面，《座头鲸之歌》帮助推动了一场初生的反捕鲸运动。豪泽说：“（它）让普通人在自己家里就能听到鲸鱼的声音。你不需要成为科学家就会被它打动。”在日益增长的压力下，1972年，美国国会通过了《海洋哺乳动物保护法》，1982年又通过了一项具有法律约束力的全球商业捕鲸禁令，随后在1985至1986年全面禁止捕鲸。一些鲸鱼的数量开始增加，尤其是座头鲸此后出现了显著恢复。在一些地方，它们现在甚至以数百头一次的超级群体出现。

##段落
鲸歌的发现是当时环保主义和动物智能认识更广泛革命的一部分。蕾切尔·卡森于1962年出版了《寂静的春天》，审视合成农药对环境的影响。1970年首个地球日动员了约2000万人，而简·古道尔和黛安·福西等科学家则忙于改变我们对其他高智商灵长类动物的认识。布丽说，鲸歌开始被视为更广泛生态危机的象征，甚至是“自然界一方哀伤的恳求”。

##段落
但到了20世纪70年代末，美国流行文化对鲸鱼或其歌声这类真诚环保象征变得更加冷嘲热讽，他们补充说，随后在80年代，鲸歌又被采纳为新世纪音乐的关键音效。布里奇补充道，即使在今天，它在很大程度上仍被视为一种缓解白领生活压力的放松剂。与此同时，罗根表示，鲸歌的发现帮助启动了此前研究薄弱的现代鲸类生物学。凯蒂发现，同一区域的所有雄性会唱大致相同的歌——而且这首歌会随时间演变。我们现在知道，这些歌曲还能跨越极远的距离在种群间传播，有时会迅速取代当地此前流行的版本。“我们正在观察文化穿越海洋，”豪泽说。虽然座头鲸拥有鲸类中最复杂的已知歌曲（它甚至展现出人类语言的一些特征），其他鲸鱼的声音也让研究人员震惊。例如，抹香鲸以类似摩尔斯电码的咔嗒声序列（称为尾音）交谈，如今已知它们存在地区方言，而雄性还会发出单独的更慢、更深沉且极其响亮的咔嗒声。蓝鲸的巨大叫声低到人耳无法捕捉，却能传播至多1000英里（1600公里）。一些研究人员甚至试图与鲸鱼对话并破译它们在说什么。罗杰晚年也参与了这项工作。如今已有数千份鲸鱼声音和其他悦耳自然声音的录音。尽管如此，克尔认为，没有一份能完全拥有70年代那些曲目的“和声或那种迷人特质”。“它有一种绝妙的美感，这种来自深海的噼啪作响、萦绕不去的声音。”也许那个时期恰好拥有特别优美的座头鲸歌声，负责将海洋联盟从1950年代到1990年代的大量海洋哺乳动物声音收藏档案（包括凯蒂和罗杰录制的许多声音）数字化和归档的艾丽莎·怀尔说。更多类似内容：• 座头鲸正在形成超级群体 • 鲸鱼类似人类的“字母表” • 揭示世界上最神秘鲸鱼秘密的声音。怀尔仍记得小时候第一次听《座头鲸之歌》。“它非凡无比，每次我听它，都会起鸡皮疙瘩。”她说，如今鲸鱼在一种截然不同的人为噪音声景中竞争，这使得保护旧录音极为重要。“这些录音保存了时空中的特定时刻以及特定的个体，”她说。“我们可以追踪这些随时间的变化，鲸鱼如何以不同方式交流，声景本身又如何不同。”鲸鱼仍面临许多威胁，从船只……

##段落
从渔网缠绕到一些国家持续的捕鲸活动，再到噪音污染和海洋变暖。如今，四分之一的鲸鱼物种面临灭绝威胁，而1991年这一比例为七分之一。尽管如此，Hauser表示，《座头鲸之歌》“无疑是推动鲸鱼保护的重要催化剂之一”。“大多数人永远不会亲眼见到活着的座头鲸，但突然间，他们可以放上一张唱片，听到鲸鱼的歌声，”她说。“突然间，讨论不再只是‘还剩多少鲸鱼？’而是变成了‘我们正在杀害的是什么样的生命？’”

##段落
*Jocelyn Timperley是BBC科学专题团队的高级记者。

dialogs.title: At the check-in counter
dialogs.goal: 练习护照/行李/座位相关表达，从容应对值机

lines.en: Good morning. May I see your passport and booking reference, please?
lines.zh: 早上好，请出示您的护照和预订编号。

lines.en: Sure, here you are. I'd like a window seat if possible.
lines.zh: 好的，给您。如果可以的话我想要靠窗的座位。

lines.en: I can arrange that. Are you checking in any bags today?
lines.zh: 可以安排。您今天有要托运的行李吗？

lines.en: Just one suitcase. Does it meet the weight limit?
lines.zh: 就一个行李箱。它超重了吗？

lines.en: It's within the limit. Your boarding pass is ready — gate 22, boarding at 10:40.
lines.zh: 在限额内。您的登机牌好了——22 号登机口，10:40 登机。

lines.en: Great. Could you also confirm that my carry-on bag fits the cabin size requirements?
lines.zh: 太好了。您能再确认一下我的随身行李符合客舱尺寸要求吗？

lines.en: Let me check the dimensions. Yes, it fits within our standard allowance. You're all set for the cabin.
lines.zh: 让我看一下尺寸。是的，符合我们的标准限额。您的客舱行李没问题。

lines.en: Perfect. By the way, is there any chance I could get an aisle seat instead? I just realized I may need to stretch my legs.
lines.zh: 太好了。顺便问一下，我能改成过道座位吗？我刚意识到可能需要伸伸腿。

lines.en: Certainly. Let me update that for you — I've moved you to 21C, an aisle seat. No problem at all.
lines.zh: 当然可以。我来为您更新——已为您调到21C，过道座位。完全没问题。

lines.en: Thank you so much. One last thing — what time should I be at the gate?
lines.zh: 非常感谢。最后问一下，我应该在什么时间到登机口？

lines.en: Please be at the gate at least 30 minutes before boarding. Enjoy your flight, and have a wonderful trip!
lines.zh: 请在登机前至少30分钟到达登机口。祝您飞行愉快，旅途顺利！

dialogs.title: Small talk at a conference
dialogs.goal: 用自然的破冰句开启商务对话，并过渡到合作话题

lines.en: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Echo, from the consumer insights team.
lines.zh: 你好，我们好像还没见过。我是 Echo，来自消费者洞察团队。

lines.en: Nice to meet you. I work on product strategy. What brings you to this session?
lines.zh: 很高兴认识你。我做产品策略。你为什么来听这场？

lines.en: I'm exploring how AI is changing our research methods. Have you seen anything useful today?
lines.zh: 我在研究 AI 如何改变我们的研究方法。你今天有看到什么有用的吗？

lines.en: Actually, yes — a talk on real-time consumer signals. We should compare notes sometime.
lines.zh: 其实有——一个关于实时消费者信号的演讲。我们应该找个时间交流一下。

lines.en: I'd love that. Let's grab coffee after the keynote.
lines.zh: 太好了。主题演讲后我们喝杯咖啡吧。

lines.en: Sounds good. By the way, how does your team currently handle qualitative data?
lines.zh: 听起来不错。顺便问一下，你们团队目前是怎么处理定性数据的？

lines.en: We still rely heavily on manual coding, which is time-consuming. That's why I'm keen on AI-driven tools.
lines.zh: 我们还是主要靠人工编码，很耗时。所以我对 AI 驱动的工具很感兴趣。

lines.en: Interesting. We've been piloting a sentiment analysis model that might complement your workflow.
lines.zh: 有意思。我们一直在试点一个情绪分析模型，可能和你们的工作流互补。

lines.en: That sounds promising. Could you share a bit more about how it handles multilingual data?
lines.zh: 听起来很有前景。你能多分享一下它如何处理多语言数据吗？

lines.en: Sure — it's trained on several major languages, but accuracy varies. Maybe we can set up a quick demo next week.
lines.zh: 当然——它在几种主要语言上训练过，但准确率有差异。也许我们下周可以安排一个快速演示。

lines.en: Perfect. I'll bring our research lead along. Let's exchange contacts and follow up by email.
lines.zh: 完美。我会带上我们的研究负责人。我们交换一下联系方式，然后邮件跟进吧。

dialogs.title: Checking into a hotel
dialogs.goal: 掌握入住登记、特殊需求与Wi-Fi等常用句

lines.en: Good evening. Do you have a reservation under the name Lee?
lines.zh: 晚上好。请问有预订在 Lee 名下吗？

lines.en: Yes, for two nights. Is breakfast included?
lines.zh: 有的，住两晚。含早餐吗？

lines.en: It is — served from 7 to 10. Could I have a room on a higher floor, away from the elevator?
lines.zh: 含的——7 点到 10 点供应。可以安排高一点、远离电梯的房间吗？

lines.en: Certainly. Here's your key card, and the Wi-Fi password is on this slip.
lines.zh: 当然可以。这是您的房卡，Wi-Fi 密码在这张纸上。

lines.en: Thank you. Could you also confirm the checkout time for me?
lines.zh: 谢谢。另外能帮我确认一下退房时间吗？

lines.en: Checkout is at noon, but we offer a late checkout until 2 PM for an additional fee.
lines.zh: 退房时间是中午12点，不过我们可以提供延迟至下午2点的退房服务，需额外收费。

lines.en: That's good to know. I might take advantage of that. Is there a gym or pool on site?
lines.zh: 这信息很有用，我可能会用到。酒店内有健身房或游泳池吗？

lines.en: Yes, both are on the second floor, open from 6 AM to 10 PM. Towels are provided at the front desk.
lines.zh: 有的，两者都在二楼，开放时间为早上6点到晚上10点。毛巾可在前台领取。

lines.en: Perfect. One more thing — could you arrange a wake-up call at 7:30 tomorrow morning?
lines.zh: 太好了。还有一件事——能帮我安排明早7:30的叫醒服务吗？

lines.en: Of course. I've noted that for room 1208. Is there anything else you need?
lines.zh: 当然可以。我已为您记录在1208房间。还有其他需要吗？

lines.en: No, that's all for now. Thanks for your help.
lines.zh: 暂时没有了，谢谢你的帮助。

dialogs.title: Ordering with dietary needs
dialogs.goal: 清晰表达过敏/忌口，避免误会

lines.en: Welcome! Have you decided what you'd like to order?
lines.zh: 欢迎！您决定好点什么了吗？

lines.en: Not yet. I'm allergic to peanuts — could you tell me which dishes are safe?
lines.zh: 还没。我对花生过敏——能告诉我哪些菜是安全的吗？

lines.en: Of course. The grilled fish and the vegetable soup are both nut-free. I'll note the allergy for the kitchen.
lines.zh: 当然。烤鱼和蔬菜汤都不含坚果。我会在厨房单上标注过敏。

lines.en: Perfect, thank you. Could I also get that without spicy sauce?
lines.zh: 太好了，谢谢。那份可以不放辣酱吗？

lines.en: Absolutely. I'll make sure the chef prepares it with a mild seasoning instead. Would you like any appetizer to start?
lines.zh: 完全可以。我会确保厨师改用清淡调味。需要先来点开胃菜吗？

lines.en: Yes, the spring rolls look good — but are they fried in peanut oil?
lines.zh: 好的，春卷看起来不错——但那是用花生油炸的吗？

lines.en: Good question. We use canola oil for frying, so they're safe. However, the dipping sauce contains sesame paste — would you like it on the side?
lines.zh: 问得好。我们用菜籽油炸，所以是安全的。不过蘸酱含芝麻酱——需要单独放旁边吗？

lines.en: That would be great. Please keep the sauce separate, and I'll decide whether to use it.
lines.zh: 那太好了。请把酱单独放，我自己决定要不要用。

lines.en: Understood. I'll also check with the kitchen on the dessert options — the mango pudding is peanut-free, but the chocolate cake may contain traces.
lines.zh: 明白了。我还会和厨房确认甜点选项——芒果布丁不含花生，但巧克力蛋糕可能含微量。

lines.en: Thanks for being so thorough. I'll go with the mango pudding then.
lines.zh: 谢谢你这么仔细。那我就选芒果布丁吧。

lines.en: Great choice. I'll place your order now and confirm everything with the chef. Your safety is our priority.
lines.zh: 好选择。我现在下单并和厨师确认所有细节。您的安全是我们的首要任务。

dialogs.title: Talking about AI at work
dialogs.goal: 用职场商务英语表达对 AI 的看法与担忧

lines.en: Have you tried the new AI assistant? It's been a game-changer for my drafts.
lines.zh: 你试过新的 AI 助手了吗？它彻底改变了我写草稿的方式。

lines.en: I have, but I'm cautious. I double-check everything it produces.
lines.zh: 试过，但我比较谨慎。它生成的东西我都会复核。

lines.en: Fair enough. I see it as a starting point, not the final answer.
lines.zh: 有道理。我把它当作起点，而不是最终答案。

lines.en: Exactly. The human touch still matters most with our clients.
lines.zh: 没错。对咱们的客户来说，人情味依然最重要。

lines.en: That said, I've noticed it saves me at least two hours a day on research and summarization.
lines.zh: 话虽如此，我注意到它每天至少帮我在研究和总结上省下两个小时。

lines.en: I can see that. But what about accuracy? I've caught it making subtle errors in data interpretation.
lines.zh: 这我能理解。但准确性呢？我抓到过它在数据解读上犯一些很细微的错误。

lines.en: I've seen that too. That's why I always cross-reference its output with our internal reports.
lines.zh: 我也遇到过。所以我才总是拿它生成的内容和咱们内部报告做交叉核对。

lines.en: Good practice. My concern is more about long-term dependency—are we losing our own analytical skills?
lines.zh: 好习惯。我更担心的是长期依赖——我们会不会失去自己的分析能力？

lines.en: That's a valid point. I try to use it as a tool, not a crutch. I still do the critical thinking myself.
lines.zh: 这点提得很对。我尽量把它当工具，而不是拐杖。关键思考还是我自己来。

lines.en: I think we need a team guideline on when and how to use AI, especially for client-facing documents.
lines.zh: 我觉得咱们需要一份团队指南，明确什么时候、怎么用 AI，尤其是面对客户的文档。

lines.en: Agreed. Let's bring that up in next week's meeting—maybe we can draft a policy together.
lines.zh: 同意。咱们下周会上提一下——也许可以一起起草一份规范。

dialogs.title: Briefing a Descriptive Panel
dialogs.zhTitle: 为描述性感官评价小组做导入简报
dialogs.goal: 掌握主持感官评价小组时的标准指令语言与"去引导化"表达。

lines.en: Good morning, everyone. Before we start, a quick reminder: we are not looking for whether you like the sample. We are looking for what you perceive.
lines.zh: 早上好。开始之前提醒一下：我们不是要知道你喜不喜欢这个样品，而是要知道你感知到了什么。

lines.en: So we should keep preference out of it entirely?
lines.zh: 所以我们要完全把偏好排除在外？

lines.en: Exactly. Intensity, not preference. If something is very sweet and you personally hate it, the score is still high.
lines.zh: 正是。评的是强度，不是喜好。如果某样东西很甜而你个人讨厌它，分数依然要打高。

lines.en: Understood. And the order of the samples?
lines.zh: 明白了。样品顺序呢？

lines.en: Balanced and randomised, as always. Please cleanse your palate with water and the unsalted cracker between each one, and wait ninety seconds.
lines.zh: 照例是平衡随机化的。每个样品之间请用清水和无盐饼干清口，并等待 90 秒。

lines.en: What if I pick up an attribute that is not on the ballot?
lines.zh: 如果我感知到一个评分表上没有的属性怎么办？

lines.en: Write it in the open field. Honestly, those are often the most useful lines on the whole sheet.
lines.zh: 写在开放栏里。说实话，那些往往是整张表上最有价值的内容。

lines.en: Should I try to match the vocabulary we agreed on in training?
lines.zh: 我需要尽量用我们培训时统一的词汇吗？

lines.en: Use the lexicon where it fits, but do not force it. A forced term hides more than it reveals.
lines.zh: 合适的地方就用词典里的术语，但别硬套。硬套的术语掩盖的比揭示的多。

lines.en: One last thing — no discussion during evaluation. We compare notes only in the debrief.
lines.zh: 最后一点——评价过程中不要交流。我们只在总结环节比对结果。

keys.zh: 评强度，不评偏好（感官分析第一原则）
平衡随机化（样品呈送设计）

dialogs.title: Presenting Findings the Client Did Not Want
dialogs.zhTitle: 汇报一个客户不想听到的结论
dialogs.goal: 练习在坏消息中保持专业与建设性的商务表达。

lines.en: So, bottom line — does the new formulation win?
lines.zh: 所以，直接说结论——新配方赢了吗？

lines.en: Not on the measure you asked about. But I would argue you were asking about the wrong measure.
lines.zh: 在你问的那个指标上没有。但我认为，你问的可能不是该问的那个指标。

lines.en: Go on.
lines.zh: 你说。

lines.en: Overall liking is flat — statistically indistinguishable. However, the new formulation scores significantly higher on perceived care and product quality cues.
lines.zh: 总体喜好度持平，统计上无差异。但新配方在"感知到的用心程度"和"品质线索"上显著更高。

lines.en: Does that translate into anything commercial?
lines.zh: 这能转化成商业结果吗？

lines.en: It correlates strongly with repurchase intent in this category. Liking predicts the first purchase; quality cues predict the fourth.
lines.zh: 在这个品类里，它与复购意向高度相关。喜好度预测第一次购买，品质线索预测第四次。

lines.en: That is a bolder claim than I expected from you.
lines.zh: 这比我预期的你会说的话要大胆。

lines.en: It is in the appendix with the regression. I would rather show you the uncomfortable version now than the comfortable one in six months.
lines.zh: 附录里有回归结果。我宁愿现在给你看那个不舒服的版本，也不想六个月后给你看那个舒服的版本。

lines.en: Fair. What would you do if this were your decision?
lines.zh: 有道理。如果是你来定，你会怎么做？

lines.en: Ship it, but rewrite the claim. You are selling reassurance, not novelty.
lines.zh: 上市，但改掉宣称。你卖的是安心感，不是新奇感。

dialogs.title: A Tight Connection
dialogs.goal: 掌握机场改签、行李与登机口相关的高频表达。

lines.en: Excuse me, my inbound flight was delayed and I have fifty minutes to make my connection. Will I be all right?
lines.zh: 打扰一下，我来程航班延误了，中转只剩 50 分钟。来得及吗？

lines.en: It is tight but doable. Are you checked through to your final destination?
lines.zh: 有点紧但可以。您的行李是直挂到终点的吗？

lines.en: Yes, my luggage is tagged all the way through. Do I need to clear security again?
lines.zh: 是的，行李直挂到底。我需要重新过安检吗？

lines.en: You will, at the transfer point. Follow the purple signs, and mention your connection time at the desk — they can fast-track you.
lines.zh: 需要，在中转处。跟着紫色指示牌走，在柜台说明您的中转时间，他们可以帮您走快速通道。

lines.en: That is a relief. And if I miss it, what are my options?
lines.zh: 那我就放心了。万一没赶上，我有什么选择？

lines.en: You would be rebooked on the next available flight at no charge, since the delay was ours.
lines.zh: 因为延误是我们造成的，您会被免费改签到下一个有位的航班。

lines.en: Could you note my seat preference now, just in case? Aisle, towards the front.
lines.zh: 能不能现在先记下我的座位偏好，以防万一？靠走道，靠前一点。

lines.en: Noted. Here is your boarding pass. Gate B22 — boarding closes twenty minutes before departure.
lines.zh: 记下了。这是您的登机牌。B22 登机口，起飞前 20 分钟停止登机。

lines.en: Thank you. One more thing — is there anywhere to grab a quick coffee on the way?
lines.zh: 谢谢。还有一件事——路上有地方能快速买杯咖啡吗？

lines.en: There is a kiosk right past security. Honestly, with fifty minutes, I would skip it.
lines.zh: 过了安检就有个小店。不过说实话，只有 50 分钟的话，我建议您别去了。

dialogs.title: Explaining What You Do at a Dinner Party
dialogs.zhTitle: 在饭局上解释你到底是做什么的
dialogs.goal: 练习用非专业语言介绍专业工作，这是最难也最有用的能力。

lines.en: So what do you actually do? Something with market research?
lines.zh: 你到底是做什么的？跟市场调研有关？

lines.en: Sort of. I work on how products feel — taste, texture, smell — and why people prefer one over another.
lines.zh: 算是吧。我研究产品给人的感受——味道、质地、气味——以及人们为什么更偏爱其中一个。

lines.en: Wait, that is a real job? Who pays for that?
lines.zh: 等等，这是个真实存在的职业？谁会为这个付钱？

lines.en: Anyone who makes something you put in your mouth or on your skin. If two products cost the same, the one that feels right wins.
lines.zh: 任何做入口或上脸产品的公司。两个产品价格一样，感觉对的那个就赢了。

lines.en: Give me an example.
lines.zh: 举个例子。

lines.en: Sure. Think about the sound a jar makes when you first open it. That pop is engineered, and it makes the food taste fresher.
lines.zh: 好。想想第一次拧开一个罐子时的声音。那声"啵"是设计出来的，它会让食物尝起来更新鲜。

lines.en: You are telling me I have been manipulated by a lid.
lines.zh: 你是说我一直在被一个盖子操纵。

lines.en: I would say informed by a lid. Your brain uses every clue it can get, and sound is a very cheap clue.
lines.zh: 我会说是被一个盖子"告知"了。你的大脑会用上一切能拿到的线索，而声音是最廉价的一种。

lines.en: Does knowing all this ruin it for you?
lines.zh: 知道这些会不会让你失去乐趣？

lines.en: Occasionally. But mostly it does the opposite — it turns an ordinary Tuesday breakfast into something worth paying attention to.
lines.zh: 偶尔会。但大多数时候是反过来的——它让一个普通周二的早餐变成值得留意的东西。

keys.en: the one that feels right wins

keys.zh: 被操纵 / 被告知（一组有分寸感的对比）

dialogs.title: Pushing Back on an Impossible Timeline
dialogs.zhTitle: 拒绝一个不可能的排期
dialogs.goal: 练习职场中"有边界感但不对抗"的英文表达。

lines.en: We need the consumer test results by the fifteenth. Can you make that work?
lines.zh: 我们需要在 15 号前拿到消费者测试结果。你能做到吗？

lines.en: Let me walk you through what fifteenth would require, and then you can decide.
lines.zh: 我先带你过一遍 15 号意味着什么，然后你来决定。

lines.en: Okay.
lines.zh: 好。

lines.en: Recruitment alone is eight working days for this profile. That leaves two days for fieldwork and one for analysis.
lines.zh: 光是招募��类人群就要 8 个工作日。剩下 2 天做执行，1 天做分析。

lines.en: Could we shorten recruitment?
lines.zh: 招募能压缩吗？

lines.en: We could, but then we take whoever is available, and 'whoever is available' is a real bias, not a rounding error.
lines.zh: 可以，但那样我们只能要"谁有空要谁"，而"谁有空"是一个真实的偏差，不是舍入误差。

lines.en: What would you propose?
lines.zh: 你的建议是？

lines.en: Two options. A directional read on the fifteenth with a clear health warning, or a defensible result on the twenty-second.
lines.zh: 两个选项。15 号给一个方向性判断，并附明确的局限说明；或者 22 号给一个经得起挑战的结论。

lines.en: The steering committee meets on the eighteenth.
lines.zh: 指导委员会 18 号开会。

lines.en: Then take the directional read, and let me write the caveat slide myself. If someone quotes it out of context in a board deck, we both pay for it.
lines.zh: 那就用方向性判断，但局限说明那页让我自己写。如果有人把它断章取义放进董事会材料，我们两个都要付代价。

lines.en: Deal.
lines.zh: 成交。

keys.zh: 方向性判断（非定论性结论）
不是可以忽略的小误差

dialogs.title: A Room With a Problem
dialogs.goal: 练习礼貌而坚定的投诉与协商。

lines.en: Hi, I checked in about an hour ago into 704. I am afraid the room is not going to work.
lines.zh: 你好，我大约一小时前入住 704。恐怕这个房间不太行。

lines.en: I am sorry to hear that. May I ask what the issue is?
lines.zh: 很抱歉。方便问一下是什么问题吗？

lines.en: There is a persistent smell of damp, and the air conditioning is quite loud. I have an early start tomorrow.
lines.zh: 有一股持续的潮味，空调也挺吵。我明天要早起。

lines.en: Let me see what else we have. We are fairly full tonight.
lines.zh: 我看看还有什么房。今晚我们几乎满房。

lines.en: I appreciate that. I am not asking for an upgrade — just somewhere quiet and dry.
lines.zh: 我理解。我不是要求升级——只想要一个安静干燥的房间。

lines.en: I can offer you 1102. It is a similar layout, higher floor, away from the lift shaft.
lines.zh: 我可以给您 1102。户型相近，楼层更高，远离电梯井。

lines.en: That sounds much better. Could someone help me move the bags?
lines.zh: 那好多了。能安排人帮我搬一下行李吗？

lines.en: Of course. And I will note a late checkout on your booking for the inconvenience.
lines.zh: 当然。另外我会在您的订单上备注延迟退房，作为对不便的补偿。

lines.en: That is very kind — thank you for sorting it out so quickly.
lines.zh: 太贴心了——谢谢你这么快就处理好。

lines.en: You are most welcome. I will have the bellman bring up your new key shortly.
lines.zh: 不客气。我会让行李员马上把新房卡送上去。

lines.en: Perfect. I will head up now and get settled. Thanks again for your help.
lines.zh: 太好了。我现在就上去安顿。再次感谢你的帮助。

keys.en: I am not asking for an upgrade
keys.zh: 我并不是要求升级（降低对抗感）

dialogs.title: Small Talk at a Conference Coffee Break
dialogs.zhTitle: 会议茶歇上的专业闲聊
dialogs.goal: 练习从寒暄自然过渡到有价值的专业交流。

lines.en: That last session was a bit of a sales pitch, was it not?
lines.zh: 刚那场基本就是个推销吧？

lines.en: A little. Though the bit about implicit measurement was worth staying for.
lines.zh: 有一点。不过关于内隐测量的那一段还是值得留下来听的。

lines.en: Are you on the client side or agency?
lines.zh: 你是甲方还是乙方？

lines.en: Client side — I look after sensory and consumer insights for a personal care portfolio.
lines.zh: 甲方——我负责一个个护品类组合的感官与消费者洞察。

lines.en: Then you must be dealing with the AI question constantly.
lines.zh: 那你肯定天天在面对 AI 那个问题。

lines.en: Constantly. My working position is that AI is excellent before fieldwork and dangerous after it.
lines.zh: 天天。我目前的立场是：AI 在田野之前很好用，在田野之后很危险。

lines.en: That is a neat way of putting it. Where do you draw the line exactly?
lines.zh: 这个说法很精炼。你具体在哪里划这条线？

lines.en: Anything that generates hypotheses, yes. Anything that generates respondents, no.
lines.zh: 任何用来生成假设的，可以。任何用来生成受访者的，不行。

lines.en: I might steal that for my next steering group.
lines.zh: 我下次开指导会可能要借用一下这句。

lines.en: Please do. Are you around for the afternoon panel? I would be curious what you make of it.
lines.zh: 尽管用。你下午的圆桌还在吗？我挺想听听你怎么看。

keys.en: a bit of a sales pitch
where do you draw the line

dialogs.title: Moderating a Focus Group
dialogs.zhTitle: 主持一场焦点小组访谈
dialogs.goal: 练习在焦点小组中保持中立、追问而不引导、妥善处理冷场与分歧。

lines.en: Let's start simple — when you first tasted this, what was the very first thing that came to mind?
lines.zh: 咱们从简单处开始——你第一口尝到时，最先冒出来的念头是什么？

lines.en: It felt… clean? Like, not heavy on the tongue.
lines.zh: 感觉……很干净？就是说，舌头上不厚重。

lines.en: Clean — can you stay with that word for a second? What makes it feel clean versus, say, watery?
lines.zh: “干净”——你能就这个词再多说一点吗？它和所谓“寡淡”的区别在哪？

lines.en: For me clean means no aftertaste. Watery would be thin and forgettable.
lines.zh: 对我来说干净就是没有余味。寡淡则是单薄、喝完就忘了。

lines.en: Good distinction. Anyone feel something different in the aftertaste?
lines.zh: 这个区分很好。有人对余味有不同感受吗？

lines.en: There's a slight bitterness at the end. Not bad, just… present.
lines.zh: 尾段有一点苦。不讨厌，就是……存在感。

lines.en: Noted — a late bitterness. And does that bitterness make you want to take another sip, or stop?
lines.zh: 记下了——尾段苦。这种苦是让你想再喝一口，还是想停下？

lines.en: Actually it makes me curious. I'd go again.
lines.zh: 其实它让我有点好奇。我会再喝。

lines.en: Curious is interesting. So the bitterness isn't a reject signal here?
lines.zh: “好奇”这个点有意思。所以这里的苦并不是拒绝信号？

lines.en: No, it feels intentional. Like the product knows what it's doing.
lines.zh: 不是，它感觉是刻意的。像产品心里有数。

keys.en: first thing that came to mind

dialogs.title: Ordering at a Café
dialogs.goal: 掌握点单、定制规格、堂食外带与确认等待时间的日常高频表达。

lines.en: Hi! What can I get for you?
lines.zh: 您好！要点点什么？

lines.en: Could I get a medium flat white, please? With oat milk if you have it.
lines.zh: 麻烦来一杯中杯澳白，可以的话用燕麦奶。

lines.en: Sure — oat milk, medium flat white. Anything to eat?
lines.zh: 好的——燕麦奶，中杯澳白。要配点吃的吗？

lines.en: Maybe one of those almond croissants. Is it still warm?
lines.zh: 来一个那个杏仁可颂吧。现在还是热的吗？

lines.en: Just came out of the oven. Want it heated a little more?
lines.zh: 刚出炉。要再加热一下吗？

lines.en: That'd be great, thank you. And could I get that to stay, not takeaway?
lines.zh: 那太好了，谢谢。这杯我要堂食，不要外带。

lines.en: For here. Name for the cup?
lines.zh: 堂食。杯子写什么名字？

lines.en: It's Echo. How long should I expect to wait?
lines.zh: 写 Echo。大概要等多久？

lines.en: About four minutes — I'll bring it over to your table.
lines.zh: 大概四分钟——我给你送到座位上。

lines.en: Perfect, thanks so much.
lines.zh: 太好了，非常感谢。

dialogs.title: Negotiating a Specification With a Supplier
dialogs.zhTitle: 与供应商谈一份感官规格
dialogs.goal: 练习就感官规格、批次公差与交付节奏与供应商沟通，守住品质底线。

lines.en: So you want the sweetness capped at level 3 on your scale?
lines.zh: 所以你们希望甜度上限压在你们量表的 3 级？

lines.en: Level 3, and critically — no more than a half-step variance between batches.
lines.zh: 3 级，而且关键是——批次之间波动不能超过半级。

lines.en: Half a step is tight. That means we re-calibrate the line every run.
lines.zh: 半级很紧。那意味着每批我们都要重新校准产线。

lines.en: I understand the cost. But the consumer test showed anything above 3.5 drops purchase intent.
lines.zh: 成本我理解。但消费者测试显示，超过 3.5 购买意向就掉。

lines.en: Fair. What if we hold 3.0 to 3.3 and flag anything outside?
lines.zh: 合理。那我们控制在 3.0 到 3.3，超出的做标记，行吗？

lines.en: That works, as long as the flag triggers a hold, not a shipment.
lines.zh: 可以，前提是标记触发的是“扣留”，不是“发货”。

lines.en: Agreed — out-of-band goes to quarantine, not the truck.
lines.zh: 同意——超范围的进待检区，不上车。

lines.en: And lead time? We can't promise the same volume if batches fail.
lines.zh: 那交期呢？如果批次出问题，我们给不了同样产量。

lines.en: We'll build in a 10% buffer stock. You get first refusal on it.
lines.zh: 我们会留 10% 缓冲库存。你们有优先调配权。

lines.en: Good. Let's put the tolerance in writing before pilot.
lines.zh: 好。试点前我们把公差写进合同。

dialogs.title: Getting Directions on the Street
dialogs.goal: 掌握问路、确认距离、交通方式切换与表达感谢的实用句型。

lines.en: Excuse me, is the metro station far from here?
lines.zh: 打扰一下，地铁站离这儿远吗？

lines.en: Which one? There are two within walking distance.
lines.zh: 哪个站？步行范围内有两个。

lines.en: The one near the museum — line 4, I think.
lines.zh: 博物馆旁边那个——应该是 4 号线。

lines.en: That's about a ten-minute walk, straight down this street, then left at the church.
lines.zh: 走过去大概十分钟，沿这条街一直走，到教堂左转。

lines.en: Straight, then left at the church. And is it signposted?
lines.zh: 一直走，教堂左转。那儿有路牌指示吗？

lines.en: Mostly. But the sign's small — look up, not at the shops.
lines.zh: 基本有。但牌子小——抬头看，别盯店铺。

lines.en: Got it. Could I take a bus instead, if I get lost?
lines.zh: 明白了。万一迷路，我能坐公交吗？

lines.en: Bus 11 stops right there. But walking's quicker at this hour.
lines.zh: 11 路公交就在那儿停。不过这会儿走路更快。

lines.en: Perfect, I'll walk. Thank you, you saved me.
lines.zh: 太好了，我走过去。谢谢你，帮了大忙。

lines.en: No problem — enjoy the museum.
lines.zh: 不客气——博物馆好好玩。

dialogs.title: Scheduling a Meeting by Email
dialogs.goal: 练习礼貌提议时间、协调多人日程、提前同步议程与跟进。

lines.en: Hi Mark, hoping to sync on the Q3 research plan — do you have 30 minutes next week?
lines.zh: Mark 你好，想就三季度研究计划对齐一下——下周你有 30 分钟吗？

lines.en: Wednesday looks open. Morning your time?
lines.zh: 周三好像有空。你那边上午？

lines.en: Wednesday 10am works. Should we include Lena from insights?
lines.zh: 周三上午十点可以。要把洞察部的 Lena 也拉上吗？

lines.en: Yes, she owns the consumer data. Send the invite and I'll add her.
lines.zh: 要，消费数据是她负责的。你发邀约，我来加她。

lines.en: Done. I'll share the agenda beforehand so we don't wander.
lines.zh: 发了。我会提前发议程，免得跑题。

lines.en: Please do — last time we spent 20 minutes on the wrong slide.
lines.zh: 务必——上次我们拿错幻灯片耗了 20 分钟。

lines.en: Noted. I'll keep it to three points: scope, timeline, owners.
lines.zh: 记下了。我控制三个点：范围、时间线、责任人。

lines.en: That's the Mark I like. Anything you need from me before?
lines.zh: 这才对味。会前你需要我做什么？

lines.en: Just your take on the budget ceiling. I don't want to over-promise.
lines.zh: 就你对预算上限的看法。我不想过度承诺。

lines.en: I'll send a one-liner by Tuesday. Talk Wednesday.
lines.zh: 周二前我发一句话给你。周三聊。
